title: Docs Viewer Runtime Ownership And Site Projection Delivery
summary: Move canonical public Docs Viewer runtime code outside site and maintain its tracked deployment projection through an internal development build.
content_html:
Docs Viewer Runtime Ownership And Site Projection Delivery

Requirements

This is the proposed first delivery of Scope, Data, And Site Foundations. Its complete result is that shared/public Docs Viewer runtime code has one canonical owner outside site/, while site/docs-viewer/ retains the exact tracked code projection required by local public-site preview and GitHub Pages.

Developers edit only canonical shared/public runtime code outside site/. Local Manage and Review routes serve that canonical code directly, while local public-site preview and GitHub Pages serve the tracked projection at the existing URLs. Canonical runtime and projected site/ changes are reviewed and committed together as one code delivery.

The projection must be deterministic, idempotent, safe to rerun, and explicit about every destination it owns. It must not copy management-only code or private configuration into the public artifact. The initial projection must be byte-identical to the current public runtime so this ownership cutover does not change visible behavior.

This is an internal code-development mechanism, not a Docs Viewer user process. It must not expose an Update Site action or become part of document Build, Publish, Deploy Repo, or Deploy Public. It preserves the public /docs-viewer/... URL contract and the current Analysis route.

This delivery does not move or change scope source, generated output, published output, public document/search payloads, public route or scope configuration, Catalogue assets, media, or route shells. It does not change scope types, implement scope Publish or document Deploy, or add Swift code.

Process

The repository-internal developer command is bin/site-code-update, backed by site-tools/site_code_update.py and an explicit projection manifest under site-tools/config/. The command writes only the tracked runtime code destinations owned by that manifest. bin/site-code-update --check verifies the same mapping without writing.

It is a delivery gate only when a change touches canonical code represented in the site-code manifest. It is not a gate for ordinary document edits, scope Build, Publish or Deploy, Catalogue-only work, or unrelated repository changes.

The normal sequence is:

edit canonical runtime
  -> test Manage and Review against canonical code
  -> run bin/site-code-update
  -> inspect the tracked site/ delta
  -> run bin/site-code-update --check
  -> run projection and public-site validation
  -> perform local public-site preview when warranted
  -> commit canonical and projected code together

Tests that exercise canonical Manage or Review code can run before projection. Projection checks, deploy-root validation, and local public-site preview run after projection because they consume tracked site/. If testing or review causes another canonical runtime change, rerun bin/site-code-update and the affected post-projection evidence before closeout.

The gate is complete when the canonical runtime and tracked site projection match exactly and appear in the same delivery diff. The command is not exposed in Docs Viewer and is not part of the user-facing document lifecycle.

Deliverables

New And Changed Files

Path or family Change
bin/site-code-update New repository-internal command wrapper with write behavior and a --check mode.
site-tools/site_code_update.py New deterministic projection implementation. It loads the maintained mapping, copies atomically, reports additions/changes/removals, and deletes stale files only within owned destinations.
site-tools/config/site-code-update.json New explicit canonical-to-site projection manifest for the JavaScript and stylesheet families in this delivery.
site-tools/tests/test_site_code_update.py New focused coverage for complete copying, check-mode drift, stale-file removal, idempotence, unrelated-file preservation, and public/private exclusion.
docs-viewer/runtime/js/public/ and docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/ New canonical homes for the corresponding runtime currently under site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/.
docs-viewer/runtime/js/reports/docs-viewer-public-reports.js New canonical home for the public report runtime currently projected under site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/reports/.
docs-viewer/static/css/{docs-viewer.css,docs-viewer-theme.css,docs-viewer-reports.css} New canonical homes beside the existing local-only Docs Viewer stylesheets.
site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/{public,shared,reports}/ and site/docs-viewer/static/css/ Existing tracked deployment destinations, thereafter written only by the internal projection for the files in its manifest. Public paths and module URLs remain unchanged.
docs-viewer/services/docs_viewer_service.py and docs-viewer/services/docs_public_mermaid_producer.py Read canonical runtime and theme code rather than treating projected site/ files as local authority. Any further direct consumers confirmed by readiness receive the same cutover.
site-tools/site_tools/validation.py and site-tools/config/site-tools.json Validate that the tracked projection matches canonical code and contains no management-only assets; retire the old duplicate JavaScript inventory in favour of the site-code manifest.
.github/workflows/public-site.yml Add canonical runtime paths to its pull-request path filter; keep manual public deployment and the workflow's non-mutating behavior unchanged.
.github/workflows/source-lint.yml and maintained lint targets Retain existing docs-viewer/runtime/js/** coverage and add the newly canonical stylesheet paths required by the final source boundary.
Existing Docs Viewer runtime, static-asset, search, report, lint, and projection contract tests Change source-level expectations to canonical paths and retain deploy-root expectations against tracked site/. Readiness confirms the exact affected files before implementation.
Durable Docs Viewer runtime and source-tree documentation Describe canonical runtime, internal projection, local canonical serving, public preview, and deployment; remove statements that identify projected runtime files as code authority.

No document, search, media, Catalogue, scope, public-route, or public-browser-config data changes in this delivery. Runtime configuration and document deployment remain owned by later stages.

Processes To Be Run

  • Relocate the shared/public JavaScript and stylesheet files to their canonical paths without changing their initial bytes, public URLs, or relative module relationships.
  • Cut local runtime consumers over to canonical paths with no fallback to site/.
  • Implement and exercise bin/site-code-update in write and check modes against only the manifest-owned destinations.
  • Generate and inspect the tracked site/ projection, confirming that unrelated site-owned artifacts remain untouched.
  • Run focused canonical-source tests, projection tests, public/private runtime-boundary checks, maintained lint for the changed source boundary, and deploy-root validation.
  • Run local Manage and Review checks against canonical code and, when warranted, local public-site preview against the projected code.
  • Update the pull-request path filters and durable documentation owners named above.
  • Review canonical and projected changes as one bounded development diff before commit and closeout.

No compatibility alias or fallback may allow local code to keep reading canonical runtime from site/. The tracked projection remains because it is deployed code, not as an alternate source tree.

Delivery Steps

1.0 — Readiness

  • [x] Confirm the complete shared/public JavaScript and stylesheet projection and the current producer and consumer of each file family.
  • [x] Confirm that the proposed canonical destinations preserve relative module relationships and do not collide with local-only modules.
  • [x] Record the current bytes of the managed runtime projection and the public/private runtime boundary.
  • [x] Confirm the implementation sequence and stop if a required change would move document data or configuration, redesign scope behavior, add a user-facing site operation, or broaden the projection beyond the named runtime code paths.

Gate: present the confirmed code projection boundary, credible blast radius, verification budget, and any required change to these deliverables before editing runtime or tooling.

1.0 Readiness Evidence — 30 August 2026

The current tracked projection is 65 ordinary tracked files: 3 public JavaScript modules, 58 shared JavaScript modules, 1 public report loader, and 3 shared/public stylesheets. No script currently produces them; developers edit these files directly under site/, site-tools/config/site-tools.json independently inventories the 62 JavaScript modules, local Docs Viewer serves the shared/public JavaScript and CSS from site/, the public Mermaid producer reads the theme there, and public preview and GitHub Pages serve the same paths directly. The proposed canonical docs-viewer/runtime/js/{public,shared}/, focused public report file, and three docs-viewer/static/css/ targets do not exist or collide with local-only modules. Moving each family as a unit preserves its relative imports, including local-only lazy imports that resolve only through the local service.

The ordered relative-path-and-byte baselines are public 39fd6b45dbd32eccc481b5d225ef2ede27f14c67c397f5b99e1112338cf0ca8a, shared c9d1a7e7527bb437c25afd973b0f7fa3de0f1c3415ed0cca2f29bc4fe6b68388, reports a122c767b21a10b1368180ac97034a46e9be7154e89225beecf9015f6911b1f3, and css 9fbf9c100566ad02ff2f84aad270c494e7d2ab0aa76eb2148d3fbb6ce5029793. The current site runtime manifest matches all 62 JavaScript files exactly, contains no management or review family, and the tracked stylesheet directory contains only the three named files. The baseline static-asset, public-runtime, and site-validation set passes 29 tests; bin/site-validate reports 62 runtime modules and the JavaScript Search contract passes.

Implementation remains the documented 1.1 through 1.5 sequence. The new projection manifest should be the single complete canonical-to-site mapping rather than leaving a second manually synchronized runtime inventory in site-tools.json; site validation consumes that mapping to check both exact public membership and byte equality. The credible production blast radius is the canonical copies, local static serving and asset versioning, public Mermaid theme input, the new site-code command and manifest, site validation, workflow path filters, maintained lint inputs, and source-level path expectations. Public shells and URLs remain unchanged, and deploy-root assertions remain against site/. Durable follow-through also includes the Development Checklist because its current public-runtime placement rule predates this approved ownership split.

Focused implementation evidence is the new projection test set; affected static-asset, public-boundary, Mermaid, Search, and report contracts; canonical and projected JavaScript lint; site validation and projection-contract audit; local Manage and Review route/service smokes; the public read-only route smoke against tracked site/; and git diff --check. No document, Search, media, scope configuration, Catalogue, Publish, deployment, or Swift file enters the mapping. Stop before 1.1 for approval.

1.1 — Canonical Runtime Cutover

  • [x] Relocate the shared/public JavaScript and stylesheets to their code-owned canonical directories.
  • [x] Update local static serving, asset versioning, lint targets, source-level tests, and code references to use those canonical paths.
  • [x] Preserve public URLs, module imports, public behavior, and management-only exclusion.

Gate: local Manage and Review load from canonical code, and the canonical public runtime graph contains the same deployable modules without depending on site/.

1.1 Evidence — 30 August 2026

The 3 public modules, 58 shared modules, focused public report loader, and 3 shared/public stylesheets now have canonical copies under docs-viewer/. All 65 canonical files remain byte-identical to the recorded 1.0 baselines and their tracked site/ counterparts. Local static routing resolves the public and shared module URLs and three shared stylesheet URLs to canonical files; the existing reports route resolves the newly canonical public loader beside local report owners. Cache versioning reads only canonical Docs Viewer JavaScript and CSS, and the public Mermaid producer reads the canonical theme. No local runtime or producer retains a site/docs-viewer/runtime/js or site/docs-viewer/static/css source read.

Source-level Search, report, CSS, route, and public-runtime contracts now inspect canonical paths. The public graph permits exactly docs-viewer-public-reports.js from the canonical reports directory and continues to reject local report, management, import, review, and source-editing modules. The maintained Docs Viewer lint scope covers 142 Python and 171 canonical JavaScript files and excludes the tracked site projection. Its first run exposed the already-retired docs-viewer/migrations root still present in lint configuration; that dead target was removed, and the fresh maintained-scope run passes.

Focused verification passes 59 Python contracts plus the JavaScript Search contract and explicit lint for the changed Python files. runtime-ownership-1-1-rerun passes all 6 Docs Viewer smoke-profile steps: canonical source lint, site validation, external-local Mermaid, local Manage, local Review, and public read-only runtime. The projection-contract audit and git diff --check pass. Public URLs, relative imports, route shells, tracked site/ bytes, document and Search payloads, scope configuration, Publish, and GitHub Pages behavior are unchanged. No site-code-update command, projection manifest, site validation integration, or workflow change from 1.2 or 1.3 has started. Stop before 1.2 for approval.

1.2 — Internal Site Projection

  • [x] Implement bin/site-code-update, site-tools/site_code_update.py, and the explicit manifest with write and consistency-check behavior.
  • [x] Project only runtime JavaScript and stylesheets into their existing tracked site/ destinations.
  • [x] Prove that the initial projection preserves current bytes, a second write is a no-op, bin/site-code-update --check detects drift, stale managed files are removed, and unrelated site files are untouched.
  • [x] Keep canonical and projected runtime changes together in the normal development diff and commit boundary.

Gate: review the exact canonical-to-deployment mapping and tracked generated delta before accepting the projection owner.

1.2 Evidence — 30 August 2026

bin/site-code-update now loads one maintained manifest and supports a default write plus read-only --check. The manifest owns four flat canonical-to-deployment mappings: 3 public JavaScript modules, all 58 shared JavaScript modules, only docs-viewer-public-reports.js from the mixed reports directory, and only the 3 named shared/public stylesheets from the mixed stylesheet directory. Fixed policy validation rejects changed roots, incomplete public/shared inventories, management report modules, local-only stylesheets, nested filenames, symlinked sources, and unsafe destination entries.

Planning compares canonical and projected bytes, reports additions, changes, and removals, replaces added or changed files atomically, and deletes unexpected files only inside the four owned deployment directories. The focused eight-test set proves complete copying, non-writing drift detection, bounded stale removal, unrelated site/assets/ preservation, a no-op second write, public/private exclusion, unsafe destination rejection, and symlinked-source rejection. The complete site-tools/tests directory passes 17 tests, the related site-validation and maintained-lint contract set passes 20 tests, and the maintained Site Tools lint scope passes all 5 Python files.

On the repository itself, bin/site-code-update --check, the initial write, a second write, and the closing check each report 0 added, 0 changed, 0 removed, 65 unchanged. The exact tracked delta under site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/ and site/docs-viewer/static/css/ is empty, confirming that adopting the projection owner changes no deployed byte. git diff --check passes. No document, Search, media, Catalogue, scope configuration, management-only asset, site validation, or workflow integration entered 1.2. Stop before 1.3 for approval.

1.3 — Development And Validation Integration

  • [x] Make the local Codex handoff the primary gate: after changing canonical runtime code, run bin/site-code-update, inspect the tracked site/ delta, and finish with local consistency and deploy-root checks before presenting work for commit.
  • [x] Make bin/site-validate, already exercised by the maintained local smoke profiles, consume the site-code manifest and reject incomplete canonical inventory, projection byte drift, extra public runtime files, and management-only assets.
  • [x] Record the canonical edit and projection sequence in repository instructions so future local Codex tasks receive it automatically, and retain maintained source checks against canonical JavaScript and stylesheets rather than the tracked projection.
  • [x] Keep pull-request integration as a secondary Codex Cloud safeguard: retain Source Lint coverage for canonical JavaScript and stylesheets and trigger Public Site validation for the canonical runtime paths.
  • [x] Preserve manual deployment as the normal public-release operation and keep the GitHub Pages workflow non-mutating: validation may reject the committed site/ snapshot but never generates or commits it.

Gate: the normal local handoff rejects a stale or unsafe projection without external scope access; the occasional pull-request path applies the same non-mutating check as a secondary safeguard.

1.3 Evidence — 30 August 2026

The repository instructions now identify canonical shared/public Docs Viewer code under docs-viewer/, the tracked site/docs-viewer/ deployment projection, and the normal local handoff sequence: run bin/site-code-update, inspect the exact tracked delta, then run bin/site-code-update --check and bin/site-validate before presenting the work for commit. Inventory or public-status changes require an explicit manifest edit, while local-only files in the mixed reports and stylesheet directories remain excluded. This is the primary guard for the ordinary local Codex-to-user commit workflow.

bin/site-validate now loads site-tools/config/site-code-update.json directly. The former 62-module JavaScript inventory has been removed from site-tools/config/site-tools.json, leaving one projection owner for all 65 files. Validation exercises the manifest's complete canonical-source checks, compares every projected byte, checks exact membership within each owned destination, scans the complete public runtime tree for files outside the manifest, rejects unsafe entries, and reports 65 projected code files including 62 JavaScript modules. Focused coverage proves stale-byte, missing-stylesheet, extra-management-module, and incomplete-canonical-inventory failures. The current tracked site passes without external scope access.

Source Lint already owned canonical docs-viewer/runtime/js/**; its secondary pull-request filter now also includes the three canonical shared/public stylesheets. Public Site pull requests are triggered by the complete public/shared source directories, the focused public report loader, the three projected stylesheets, the site-code command, tooling, or tracked site/. That workflow continues to run validation only: it neither generates nor commits the projection, and manual deployment remains unchanged.

The focused integration set passes 47 tests. runtime-ownership-1-3-source-lint passes all 6 maintained source scopes, and runtime-ownership-1-3 passes all 6 Docs Viewer smoke steps: canonical source lint, manifest-backed site validation, external-local Mermaid, local Manage, local Review, and public read-only runtime. Both workflow YAML files parse, bin/site-code-update --check reports 0 added, 0 changed, 0 removed, 65 unchanged, the tracked runtime and stylesheet delta under site/ is empty, and git diff --check passes. Stop before 1.4 for approval.

1.4 — Code Review

  • [x] Review the bounded source, projection tooling, service, validation, test, documentation, and generated-site diff for split ownership, duplicate producers, compatibility residue, unsafe deletion scope, hidden site/ reads, and accidental public management assets.
  • [x] Resolve findings and rerun only the evidence affected by review changes.

Gate: present the reviewed change set and focused evidence for approval before closeout.

1.4 Evidence — 30 August 2026

The review covered the complete delivery diff from the accepted 1.0 readiness commit through the committed 1.1–1.3 implementation and the 1.4 working changes. The canonical service routes, asset versioning, Mermaid theme producer, source-level tests, maintained lint, projection command, validation, workflow filters, and tracked deploy roots now agree on the ownership split. The site-code manifest is the sole maintained 65-file canonical-to-deployment inventory and the sole producer is bin/site-code-update; validation consumes that manifest rather than maintaining another list. Executable references to site/docs-viewer/runtime/js or site/docs-viewer/static/css are confined to projection policy and lint exclusions. Deploy-root tests continue to inspect site/ deliberately. Older durable documents that still describe the former code locations are the named 1.5 documentation work, not runtime fallbacks.

Review found and resolved two bounded issues. First, application previously relied on the planner to confine deletion. It now validates the complete actionable plan before writing: copies must match an exact manifest source and destination, removals must be direct stale files inside a manifest-owned destination and must not be current targets, and duplicate actionable targets are rejected. A regression test proves that a forged removal under unrelated site/assets/ is rejected without touching the file. Second, the canonical docs-viewer.css and docs-viewer-reports.css headers still named their former site/ locations. Those comments now name the canonical paths, and the normal projection workflow produced exactly the corresponding two tracked stylesheet changes. No runtime CSS declaration or visible behavior changed.

The final public projection contains exactly 62 JavaScript modules and 3 stylesheets; filename and manifest audits find no management, Review, Import, source-editing, or local-only asset. The affected focused set passes 42 tests, including 9 projector tests and the manifest-backed site-validation and canonical/static public-boundary contracts. runtime-ownership-1-4-review passes all 6 Docs Viewer smoke steps, and runtime-ownership-1-4-review-source-lint passes all 6 maintained source scopes. A second projection write and bin/site-code-update --check each report 0 added, 0 changed, 0 removed, 65 unchanged; bin/site-validate reports 65 projected files and 62 runtime modules; the projection-contract audit and git diff --check pass. Stop before 1.5 for approval.

1.5 — Closeout

  • [x] Confirm that the complete runtime-ownership and projection result works while document Build, Publish, deployment, scope storage, and GitHub Pages behavior remain unchanged.
  • [x] Update the durable documentation owners and record any separate Stage 2 prerequisite discovered during implementation.
  • [x] Recommend whether this delivery document should be retained for review or retired after its stable conclusions have moved to durable documentation.

Gate: close only after the user accepts the shipped outcome and the feature points clearly to the next scope Build and Publish delivery rather than extending this one.

1.5 Closeout Evidence — 30 August 2026

The accepted implementation through 1.4 is committed at f790eaae7. Current durable documentation now states the ownership split at its actual owners: Development Checklist records the normal local handoff and explicit manifest-change rule; Run Checks owns the projection commands and evidence scope; Source Tree Ownership distinguishes canonical Docs Viewer code, site-owned public assets, and the tracked runtime projection; and the Docs Viewer overview, runtime/module map, and public-preview guidance identify canonical paths, unchanged public URLs, and local-versus-static serving. Only these current owner and routing documents were updated; older delivery and feature records remain historical rather than being mechanically rewritten. The Docs watcher produced their expected by-ID payloads plus recent and backlinks projections, without a Search rebuild.

The complete Stage 1 diff contains no change under Docs Viewer builders, scope/default/route configuration, public document data, or Studio data. Existing document Build, Publish, scope storage, deployment, and public payload composition therefore retain their owners and behavior; Stage 1 does not implement Deploy Repo or Deploy Public. The GitHub Pages workflow change adds canonical runtime paths to pull-request validation and renames the validation step; its build, upload, and deploy commands remain unchanged and non-mutating. Public URLs and the Analysis route are unchanged. Accepted 1.4 evidence remains the proportional runtime proof: 42 affected tests, both 6-step smoke/lint profiles, manifest-backed site validation, projection contract, and whitespace validation all pass.

Closeout checks confirm 0 added, 0 changed, 0 removed, 65 unchanged, site validation reports 65 projected files and 62 runtime modules, the projection-contract audit passes, and git diff --check passes. No separate Stage 2 prerequisite was discovered. The parent feature's existing requirement still applies: before repository-backed canonical Markdown moves to external scope storage, Stage 2 must define the minimum recoverable snapshot boundary and accept the migration order. The runtime code manifest must not be expanded into a document Build, Publish, or deployment mechanism.

Recommendation: retain this delivery through final Stage 1 acceptance and its normal user commit so its bounded evidence remains reviewable, then retire it from the normal documentation set once the parent feature points to an accepted Stage 2 delivery. Its stable ownership and workflow conclusions now live in durable documentation. The document remains in-progress until the user accepts this closeout and explicitly decides whether to retain or retire it.
